chapter_title: [Concer]ning why, if the Person shall look down in

fills.notes: The sentence needs a causal bridge: “Sin[ce] … in this way it cast itself down …”. The oldest-layer register is impersonal explanation: “Since it caused (this), in this way it cast itself down…”. Restoring a verb of causation keeps the correspondence tight: the inversion in water is an effect caused by the Summons’ descent.

fills.fill: from the height into the depth
fills.notes: The image requires a discrete-degree descent (above→below) to match the correspondence: the Summons ‘sent down’ to the worlds of Darkness, therefore it ‘casts itself down’ from height to depth, like a diver. This also prepares ¶4’s answering ascent (obedience from below upward).

Balances the clause structure: when disturbed, the person ‘raises’ the shadow’s appearance upward (i.e., it stands out/lengthens on the earth), which the following line contrasts with what is impossible to do in actuality.

Continues the observable phenomenon: the shadow appears ‘stretched out’/projected upon the earth ‘above’ (i.e., outward/forward from the feet). This keeps the focus on the shadow’s dependence and inversion relative to the body.

The next line reads: “It is impossible for him to do [X] on the earth.” In the correspondence, the body cannot make its own shadow ‘stand’ independently; the shadow is an effect tied to the earth/light. Hence: impossible for him ‘to do his shadow to stand’ (i.e., to set it upright/free).

assessment: Most bracketed items are straightforward letter-completions. The main recoveries are ¶3 (causal verb + descent phrase) and ¶7 (shadow-behavior clauses). Those are constrained by the chapter’s inside→outside correspondence: descent (Summons) produces inversion in the reflective ‘sea’; ascent (Obedience) removes the face from visibility; the shadow section must express the same dependence of effects on their lower plane (earth/abyss) and the impossibility of reversing that dependence by one’s own power.
